modalLead: A custom widget can be tried before it is saved. Ask the address from the settings panel and see the answer that comes back — the whole document, beside the figures your paths make of it — and keep watching it while a queue drains or a service comes back up.

items.text: Try a custom widget before saving it. The tile was the only place its answer was ever visible, and all a tile can say about a path that matched nothing is — four of those look the same whether the address is wrong, the key is wrong, or the JSON simply nests a level deeper than your boxes say. Config → Widgets → Settings now has a Try it block: Ask now makes the very request the widget describes and shows what came back, indented and in the service's own order, beside the figures your paths read out of it. Above both sit the facts — method, host, status, how long it took, how much arrived, and whether a sign-in went with it, which is the difference between a wrong key and no key at all. Asking saves nothing.

Keep watching, and see what moves. The same request every 5, 10, 30 or 60 seconds, with the figures that changed on the last beat marked for a moment — for a queue draining or a machine coming back up while you are looking at it. It asks nothing while the tab is in the background, and stops itself after five minutes rather than quietly polling somebody's service all afternoon.

GET or POST is a setting again. nextDash has always accepted both and the manual always said so, but the panel offered neither — the only way to give a widget POST was to edit its stored file by hand. It is a dropdown beside the address now. Nothing is sent with either: POST is for the services that answer a statistics endpoint on that method and no other.
